newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan import tariffs depress Taiwan pork prices.
newsitem.headline: Japan import tariffs depress Taiwan pork prices.

text.p: Taiwan pork prices have fallen more than 40 percent from a June 1996 high, depressed primarily by import tariffs imposed by Japan, Council of Agriculture officials said on Wednesday.
Taiwan's average wholesale pork price fell to around T$42 per kg on Wednesday from a peak of T$72 per kg in early June, an official of the cabinet agency said.
Council officials attributed the sharp fall primarily to Japan's reimposition on July 1 of a pork import tariff at a time of generally strong domestic production.
An Economics Ministry official said Taiwan's agriculture exports to Japan, with pork as the largest item, plunged in October to US$170 million from US$250 million in October 1995,
Comparative October export values for pork were not available, but the official confirmed that the year-on-year decline was attributable chiefly to Japan's falling imports.
Of Taiwan's 266,757 tonnes of pork exports in 1995, 183,494 tonnes went to Japan, the island's largest pork market.
Taiwan was Japan's top source of 1995 pork imports.
